songs_to_prepare.title: I'm Still Here

songs_to_prepare.title: Rose's Turn

company/company-joanne.style_guidance: Joanne is sharp, witty, and devastatingly perceptive — alto/mezzo with a razor-edged belt and absolute command of a room. She is the most dangerous person at the party.

songs_to_prepare.title: Losing My Mind
songs_to_prepare.why: A woman whose passion for her husband overwhelms her — obsessive, aching, mezzo-soprano

songs_to_prepare.title: So Many People

company/company-sarah.style_guidance: Sarah is a bundle of contradictions — warmth and rage, the karate subplot says it all. Mezzo-soprano who can flip between sweetness and teeth.
avoid: One-dimensional nice-wife material — Sarah is fighting something enormous inside herself

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Loved You
songs_to_prepare.why: Lyric baritone showing a man tangled up in what he wants but cannot quite say

songs_to_prepare.title: Old Friend

company/company-harry.style_guidance: Harry is a secondary couple character — warm baritone presence, gently comedic, the 'relaxed' partner who isn't as relaxed as he seems.
avoid: Show-stopping material — Harry is a supporting role, understated is the note

company/company-amy.style_guidance: Amy is a comedic soprano set piece — the patter requires absolute technical mastery. Cast someone who can nail Getting Married Today and then show heart underneath it.

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky

songs_to_prepare.title: Some Enchanted Evening

company/company-paul.style_guidance: Paul is Amy's devoted, slightly bewildered partner — warm baritone sincerity. The steady one in a chaotic relationship.

songs_to_prepare.title: The Road You Didn't Take
songs_to_prepare.why: A man contemplating choices with a carefully managed sense of peace — secondary couple character

songs_to_prepare.title: Take Me to the World
songs_to_prepare.why: Gentle, reflective baritone — ideal for the quieter Company husbands

company/company-peter.style_guidance: Peter is a secondary couple husband — warm, present, slightly enigmatic. Supporting baritone role.

songs_to_prepare.title: Losing My Mind
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo-soprano in a complicated marriage — aching, searching quality

songs_to_prepare.title: What I Did for Love

company/company-susan.style_guidance: Susan is moving to Arizona — she has made a decision. Mezzo-soprano with ground beneath her feet, even if her marriage is complicated.
avoid: Showy material — Susan is quiet revelation, not spectacle

songs_to_prepare.title: So Many People
songs_to_prepare.why: Early Sondheim mezzo — warm, domestic, with complexity underneath

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know
songs_to_prepare.why: Warm mezzo character moment — a woman who observes and understands

company/company-jenny.style_guidance: Jenny is the pot-smoking wife who is more relaxed than she appears — mezzo warmth with a surprise turn. Secondary role, but the surprise moment is memorable.

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: Baritone with understated masculine vulnerability — the quiet one in the couple

songs_to_prepare.title: Willkommen
songs_to_prepare.why: Ensemble/character baritone energy — good for showing personality without leading-man weight

company/company-david.style_guidance: David is a secondary couple husband with minimal solo material — warm, present baritone. The role is about ensemble chemistry.

songs_to_prepare.title: A Little Bit in Love

songs_to_prepare.title: Finishing the Hat

songs_to_prepare.why: A person who understands what it costs to be with someone like Bobby — mezzo intelligence

songs_to_prepare.title: The Road You Didn't Take

songs_to_prepare.title: Waving Through a Window

diary-of-a-wimpy-kid/wimpy-mrs-clayton.style_guidance: Mrs. Clayton is a supporting adult female character — warm mezzo presence with comic awareness. Secondary role.
